Seminar Title:

A Functional Safety SoC for Industrial IoT

Seminar Type:

Registration Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

Bodasingi Sai Surya Murali Dhar ( Rollno : 524ec2015)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

EC 303 Seminar Room

Date and Time:

05 Nov 2026 17:15

Contact:

Ayas Kanta Swain

Abstract:

Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems depend on sensor networks to monitor and control industrial processes, and a failure in such a system can cause high-risk losses. A safety function can act correctly only on correct data, so an undetected sensor or hardware fault can stop it from reaching the safe state. Detecting faults, and measuring how many of them are detected, is therefore central to functional safety under IEC 61508. Existing studies report fault detection accuracy rather than the diagnostic coverage (DC), safe failure fraction (SFF) and safety integrity level (SIL) required by the standard, treat network quality and sensor health separately, and rely on safety processors that are either closed or lack a safety manager and FMEDA. This work aims to develop an open functional safety system-on-chip (SoC) for an IIoT wireless sensor network, in which the sensor data, the node hardware and the network decision are protected together and assessed on measured data. The approach compares statistical fault detection methods with a proposed normalised score on real sensors under hardware fault injection, applies lightweight anomaly detection and quality-of-service measurement at the network edge, and builds a generic safety subsystem with a health-aware 2oo3 voter around the open Ibex RISC-V core, followed by FMEDA of the complete chain. A review of 34 journal papers and vendor documents shows that explainable one-class methods suit the edge better than deep learning, and that lockstep and ECC have so far been validated only at the processor level. An I2C interface for the ADT7420 sensor and an APB&ndashI2C FIFO subsystem have been built and verified on FPGA, and data collection from a two-sensor test setup has started. The work is expected to give an open design and measured evidence for assessing the safety of a complete IIoT sensing chain under IEC 61508.
